From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Quick follow-up + procurement next steps (vendor packet, PO vs card)

Hi Travis / Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time on the call today — great to learn more about Orion Finance's use cases for internal knowledge search and customer service summarization. As discussed, wanted to follow up with the immediate procurement items so your finance team can move this along: 

1) Vendor intake: Do you have a preferred vendor intake form or portal? If so, can you share the Procurements intake PDF/link and any required fields?

2) PO vs card: Will this be paid via purchase order (Net terms) or corporate card? We can accept both; if you need Net30/Net45, we (Redwood) typically process via PO + vendor packet.

3) Attachments: I'm attaching our standard vendor packet, W-9, and bank info stub for vendor setup. If your team requires anything different (W-8, tax forms, certificate of insurance), let me know and I'll loop in our legal/accounts.

4) Marketplace / vendor portal: Are you planning to procure via a marketplace (AWS Marketplace) or onboard Redwood directly into your vendor portal? If you prefer marketplace procurement, we can check listing status and provide next steps.

Next steps: If you can send the intake form + any vendor portal invite, Marissa (cc'd) from our operations team will take it from there and confirm paperwork.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0117 | dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Packet.pdf (PDF), Redwood_W-9_2026.pdf (PDF), Redwood_Vendor_Banking_Details.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Travis Miller <travis.miller@orionfinance.com>

Date: 2026-09-13T11:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + procurement next steps (vendor packet, PO vs card)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the recap. Quick answers from procurement:

- I've attached our Procurement Intake Form (see attachment). Please fill out the sections for vendor name, tax id, remit address, and contact for invoices.
- We prefer to pay by PO on Net30 for annual SaaS agreements; card is ok for pilot/proof-of-concept purchases under $5k.
- We have a vendor portal (Coupa). Do you have a vendor ID with Coupa already? If not, procurement@orionfinance.com can send an invite once we have the completed intake and W-9 plus bank account details for ACH.

Also: Can you confirm whether Redwood requires a signed master services agreement (MSA) before PO issuance, or whether a mutually-signed statement of work + PO is sufficient?

Thanks,
Travis Miller
Sr. Procurement Manager | Orion Finance
Attachment: Orion_Procurement_Intake_Form.pdf

Hey Dylan,

Thanks for looping me in. Quick operational notes:

- Intake form: We'll complete the Orion intake form once you provide the vendor packet + W-9 + bank details. I'll own submission into Coupa if they invite us.
- MSA: Standard is our Redwood MSA (v2026-03) — we can accept a signed SOW + PO for pilots, but for enterprise deals we prefer an executed MSA. If they require redlines, send over their standard MSA and I'll coordinate with Legal.
- Taxes: We only provide W-9 (US entity). If they ask for W-8, confirm entity and I'll escalate to Finance.
- Banking: I'll redact routing/account details in the email and attach the secure XLSX via our vendor portal if they require additional verification.

Let me know once you get the intake form back from them and if they request any additional certificates (COI, SOC 2 attestation). I can also pull our SOC 2 summary and PCI scope doc if needed.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
